editorial.headline: Watercraft Leasing Is Nationally Open—but Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: The national PMA position permits full foreign ownership of operator-free commercial watercraft leasing, yet Bali blocks PMA registration for this activity.
editorial.body:
**The business at the centre of the code.** Watercraft is not treated as a generic category here. This activity covers rental and operational leasing, without a purchase option, of water transport equipment supplied without an operator. The examples given are commercial ships and boats. The asset, not an operated transport service, is the subject. Water transport rented with an operator sits outside the scope; so does the rental of boats for sport and recreation, including recreational boats, canoes, sailboats, and yachts. The code therefore has a precise commercial centre: water-transport equipment made available without an operator.

**Who can register it.** The record lists Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar as the scales open to this activity. That full spread is worth noticing: it is not confined in the record to a single scale of business. Nationally, PMA status is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national setting permits the full ownership stake stated in the record. It is a national position, however, not a Bali registration clearance. The same slim record contains a separate provincial finding for Bali, which changes the practical answer for a foreign investor there.

**What changes in Bali.** For a foreigner seeking to register this activity in Bali today, the answer is no. Its Bali status is Blocked (risk class). The stated reason is specific: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope. Bali blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI through an island-wide, permanent moratorium; the record links this block to that Bali moratorium in May 2026. Under the stated provincial rule, that risk finding puts this activity behind a Bali PMA block.

That contrast is the decisive planning fact. Read only nationally, the activity is open and can carry the stated 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. Read in the Bali setting supplied here, the location changes the outcome: national openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling do not overcome Bali’s block on PMA registration. The scope remains the same—operator-free rental and operational leasing of commercial water transport equipment—but a foreign investor cannot register it for PMA in Bali today.
